greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. Peace be with you all as we gather in the light of Christ to listen to His word.
penitential:
Lord, you are the light that never fades. Lord, have mercy.
Christ, you are the river of life-giving water. Christ, have mercy.
Lord, you are the hope of those who seek your face. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: I will praise your name for ever, Lord.
homily:
We often think of the end of things as a closing of a door. We imagine the finality of a sunset, the last page of a favorite book, or the moment a traveler turns the corner and is lost to our sight. But today, the Scriptures invite us to look at the end not as a closing, but as an unfolding. In the Book of Revelation, the angel shows John a river of life-giving water, sparkling like crystal, flowing from the throne of God. It is a scene of constant, living motion. It is not stagnant. It is a river that feeds a tree whose leaves are medicine for the nations. 

I want you to hold onto this image today: the river. A river is always moving, always going somewhere, always connecting the source to the sea. Think of Benjamin Vo. Think of the way he moved through his fifteen years. He was a boy who understood the beauty of flow—the way an airplane moves through the sky, the way code runs through a system, the way a life is meant to be lived with purpose and direction. He was a boy who looked at the horizon not with fear, but with the excitement of a navigator. He was a boy who loved to dream of 'con chim airlines,' giggling at the very thought of the birds taking flight, his imagination soaring as high as the jets he spent hours spotting with his father. He was a boy who knew that life is not meant to be static; it is meant to be a journey, a movement toward something greater.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: five months have passed. The calendar page turns, but the heart often stays in the room where he last smiled. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the quick laugh, the bright smile, the way he would share his dreams—are suddenly met with an empty space. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary day. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are not a lack of faith; they are the language of love that has no place left to go.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. We wonder if we could have done more, if we could have seen further, if we could have changed the course of the river. Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. You are not to blame for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus warns his disciples: 'Beware that your hearts do not become drowsy from the anxieties of daily life, and that day catch you by surprise like a trap.' He calls us to vigilance. But what is this vigilance? It is not a state of nervous anxiety or looking over our shoulders in fear. It is a state of wakefulness to the presence of God. It is the ability to see the river of life even when the world seems dry. Think of Benjamin’s heart—that boy who, unprompted, wanted to hand over his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it; the offering itself was the testimony. It was the pure, unadulterated desire to be a blessing to someone else. That is the vigilance of the soul. That is the readiness to stand before the Son of Man. Ben’s life is a testimony that love is the only thing that survives the passage of time. The river flows, and the love we give on earth is the water that feeds the tree of life. It is purified, it is made eternal, and it is what we carry into the presence of the Lamb.

Consider the image of the river again. It flows from the throne of God. It is the very life of the Spirit. Benjamin is drinking from that river now. He is not a memory tucked away in a photo album; he is a living soul in the Banquet of Heaven. He is fully alive, fully restored, and fully embraced by the Father. He is the boy who loved to dream, the boy who giggled at the idea of his own airline, the boy who looked at the world with such profound curiosity. He is all of that, and he is with the God of the living. He is the firstfruits of the promise, waiting for the day when the family of four is whole again. He is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. He is the one who has already crossed the threshold into the light, and he is cheering you on.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart. You are the one who carries his laughter forward. You are the one who keeps the melody alive.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. The Lamb who was slain is the Lamb who is risen, and he is the one who promises that one day, every tear will be wiped away, and we will see clearly that love was the only thing that ever mattered. The God of the living is the God who is with you right now in this very room, in the silence, in the ache, and in the hope that refuses to die.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may you feel the warmth of His light upon your faces today and always. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's face.
For all families who grieve, that the Lord may console them with His peace and fill their hearts with the hope of the resurrection.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
John said:
An angel showed me the river of life-giving water,
sparkling like crystal, flowing from the throne of God
and of the Lamb down the middle of the street,
On either side of the river grew the tree of life
that produces fruit twelve times a year, once each month;
the leaves of the trees serve as medicine for the nations.
Nothing accursed will be found anymore.
The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it,
and his servants will worship him.
They will look upon his face, and his name will be on their foreheads.
Night will be no more, nor will they need light from lamp or sun,
for the Lord God shall give them light,
and they shall reign forever and ever.

And he said to me,
“These words are trustworthy and true,
and the Lord, the God of prophetic spirits,
sent his angel to show his servants what must happen soon.”
“Behold, I am coming soon.”
Blessed is the one who keeps the prophetic message of this book.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to his disciples:
“Beware that your hearts do not become drowsy
from carousing and drunkenness
and the anxieties of daily life,
and that day catch you by surprise like a trap.
For that day will assault everyone
who lives on the face of the earth.
Be vigilant at all times
and pray that you have the strength
to escape the tribulations that are imminent
and to stand before the Son of Man.”

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
